card.name: Velakali
card.tagline: Nair martial temple dance enacting a Pandava-Kaurava battle
card.profile: Velakali is an all-male martial temple dance of the Nair (traditional warrior) community of Kerala, in which performers wear the costume and colourful headgear of medieval Nair soldiers and wield swords and shields, with movements drawn from the martial art Kalarippayattu (Kerala Tourism; Wikidata). It depicts a battle between the Pandavas and Kauravas and originated in the princely state of Chempakassery (modern Ambalappuzha) under army chieftain Mathur Panicker (Kerala Tourism). It is a regular feature of the pooram at the Ambalappuzha Sree Krishna Temple and marks the start of the annual Painkuni festival at the Sree Padmanabhaswamy Temple, Thiruvananthapuram, accompanied by panchavadyam percussion (Kerala Tourism; Parampara Project).
card.insight: Velakali preserves the martial heritage of Kerala's Nair militias within a devotional temple frame, transforming choreographed swordplay into ritual offering at major temple festivals (Kerala Tourism).
